statement: Let T = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} nums[i]. For each subset S of the index set {0,...,n-1}, define sum(S) = sum_{i in S} nums[i], with the empty subset giving 0. The function returns a result r such that r >= 0 and, for every integer b with 0 <= b < 63, the b-th bit of r (that is, floor(r / 2^b) mod 2) is 1 if and only if there exists a subset S of {0,...,n-1} for which the b-th bit of sum(S) is 1. Equivalently, r is the bitwise OR of all values sum(S) over all subsets S of indices.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and for every integer i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000. Under these constraints the total sum of nums is at most 10^14, so all subset sums fit in signed 64-bit integers.
